critical_code_review_comments: server.py waitlist_status (line 3367) and admin_waitlist_action (line 3401) handle null token/sid gracefully, but admin_waitlist_action does not check whether the sub actually belongs to the admin's program context — any admin can act on any sid. Acceptable for a single-tenant staff tool but worth noting.

_yir_recipients default-ask uses `int(round(float(last.get(k) or default))) or default` — if a donor's last gift was 0 (free event tickets stored as $0?), the `or default` fallback kicks in which is actually correct for the spec. Edge case already handled.
/certificates/request rate limit of 3 per 10 min is per-IP via _rate_limit; shared office IPs could lock out legitimate users. Minor UX concern; probably fine for anti-abuse.

_cert_pdf runs PIL in a thread (good) but every request regenerates the PDF (CPU ~200ms). Since cert_token->milestone is immutable (name/threshold/date never change), consider caching PDF bytes keyed by cert_token in GridFS or Mongo for repeat downloads.
WaitlistPanel.jsx uses window.confirm for destructive actions — spec acceptable, but a shadcn <AlertDialog> would be more on-brand and keyboard-accessible (same note as iter-12 YIR send).
server.py is now ~4615 lines — repeat note from iter-11/12. Split waitlist, certificates and YIR into dedicated routers.

AdminPrograms row shows 'Waitlist' button only when p.capacity>0 (correct per spec). However, programs that have waitlisted sign-ups but currently capacity=0 (admin reduced capacity) will not show the Waitlist button, hiding existing waitlisters. Consider showing when capacity>0 OR has waitlisted subs.

ProgramSignup success screen shows 'Check my position anytime' link but the token is included as a querystring (/waitlist/status?token=...). If a user forwards the confirmation screen URL, the recipient can see the position. Low risk given the token is only a position-reveal (not claim). Document this in the UX copy or send status via email only.
